statement: Final positioning verdict: a post-hoc temporal re-ranking component cannot be positioned as a distinct contribution. Temporal scoring with decay is implemented (learnable decay inside graph retrieval), validity-aware filtering is prescribed and partially implemented (ontology-driven pre-retrieval filtering by temporal validity), the legal-retrieval review states the bitemporal/point-in-time requirement and even its detection criterion ('can the system return the text that was in force at T') but reports no benchmarked empirical comparison, and a leading legal benchmark documents that retrieval-oriented legal benchmarks do not assess whether retrieved provisions remain in force. The defensible remaining delta is therefore the implemented measurement: version-level point-in-time recovery and contamination on near-duplicate amended clauses with recency-decoupled strata, plus the comparative result on whether the published recency-decay hybrid suffices. Note that even the metric is conceptually prescribed by prior work, so novelty is implementation and evidence rather than formulation.

evidence.quote: The paper does not report a benchmarked empirical comparison of existing systems; its contribution is formal and diagnostic
can the system return the text that was in force at T
Still, it assumes the underlying corpus is normatively stable and does not assess whether retrieved provisions remain in force or have been superseded, amended, or repealed.
